findings.title: Flexible Assist rotation does not use the documented previous active week
findings.evidence: The query requires current week_start minus exactly seven days while architecture promises the previous active week. A disposable 2026-09-07 then 2026-09-21 generation retained five earlier active Assist owners but supplied an empty previous-assignment map to the second generator.
findings.triggerConditions: Generate a flexible-weekly roster after one or more skipped Monday weeks, such as a school holiday or exam break.
findings.impact: The secondary same-weekday anti-repeat input is lost across the gap. Persistent history fairness, eligibility and deterministic generation still apply; this can nevertheless repeat an AHP contrary to the documented rotation behavior.
findings.rootCause: The implementation encoded calendar adjacency while documentation later specified previous active week semantics.
findings.smallestPracticalCorrection: Obtain a policy decision. If active-week semantics are intended, query the latest draft/published week earlier than the current week with deterministic descending order and limit one. Otherwise revise the documentation and tests to say exact previous calendar week.
findings.broaderArchitecturalCorrection: None; retain the existing helper seam.
findings.regressionRisk: Medium: post-break flexible assignments can change.
findings.verificationMethod: Add Admin and Guest cases for consecutive, one-gap, multi-gap, withdrawn-only and future-week exclusion; rerun Assist, policy, persistence and release-browser gates.
findings.uncertainty: Behavior is confirmed; desired semantics require the policy owner's decision.
findings.falsePositiveNotes: Not a P1 data-corruption issue because persistent fairness and eligibility remain enforced.
findings.releaseImpact: Resolve or explicitly accept before claiming previous active week behavior.

findings.title: Current/live release truth is contradictory inside authoritative documents
findings.evidence: The same tree calls rc24 current, rc21 live/current, and rc20 live/current in active wording. The Worker package manifest remains 1.2.0-rc.24 while the exact source tree is tagged rc26.
findings.triggerConditions: A successor or incident responder uses a lower section rather than the newest banner to identify source, Worker or rollback truth.
findings.impact: Operators can choose the wrong source/host/Worker pair, misunderstand rollback order or repeat stale evidence. This proves documentation ambiguity, not a wrong production deployment.
findings.rootCause: Release tuples are copied into many prose sections and newer banners do not mechanically invalidate earlier current/live wording.
findings.smallestPracticalCorrection: After the controlled rc26 outcome is known, update every active current/live statement together and label retained older passages historical.
findings.broaderArchitecturalCorrection: Use one machine-readable current-release manifest consumed by documentation and verification tests.
findings.regressionRisk: Low application risk; medium operator-handover risk if only some copies are corrected.
findings.verificationMethod: Reject multiple active current/live tuples in documentation tests and compare the release manifest with tag, deployment report and read-only live evidence.
findings.uncertainty: The finding is bound to the audited tree. The separate task later reported rc26 live and began post-baseline documentation correction in an isolated worktree.
findings.falsePositiveNotes: Historical evidence can retain old tuples, but it must not call them current or live without a historical qualifier.
findings.releaseImpact: Documentation handoff should be corrected with the next confirmed deployment result.

findings.title: Dynamic wildcard dependency facade creates an 83-name hidden workflow interface
findings.evidence: Runtime inspection counted 83 dynamic exports and eight modules in the wildcard chain. reporting.py explicitly imports defaultdict, date, datetime and select before the wildcard import, which rebinds them to currently equivalent objects. Compilation, full tests and cycle analysis found no current runtime failure.
findings.triggerConditions: Add a non-underscore global to either facade, change import order, or add a same-named helper in a mixin.
findings.impact: Symbol ownership and dependencies are hidden; unrelated changes broaden every mixin namespace and static/refactor tooling loses precision.
findings.rootCause: An extraction convenience became a dynamic public interface rather than a fixed compatibility facade.
findings.smallestPracticalCorrection: Freeze __all__ to an explicit list, then replace wildcard imports one module at a time with the names actually used.
findings.broaderArchitecturalCorrection: Split types, persistence primitives, policy/generator APIs and utilities only if the explicit-import migration demonstrates stable seams.
findings.regressionRisk: Medium: missing implicit names may surface on less-used paths.
findings.verificationMethod: Compile, AST/static undefined-name checks, import smoke, workflow/persistence/restore/share/report tests and the full release verifier.
findings.uncertainty: No harmful current collision was found.
findings.falsePositiveNotes: This is an interface-burden finding, not proof of current symbol confusion.
findings.releaseImpact: Suitable for a separate tested maintainability batch, not an emergency release blocker.

findings.title: One record-specific backup repair failure prevents later repair attempts
findings.evidence: A disposable database with two pending obligations and a first-ID-only injected failure called only the first ID and raised. Existing tests prove that a failed startup repair keeps the workflow read-only.
findings.triggerConditions: At least two pending obligations and a failure specific to an earlier record rather than a globally unavailable backup device.
findings.impact: Later repairable obligations receive no attempt or evidence in the same run. The service remains fail-closed, making this an availability/diagnostic limitation rather than a data-loss or false-safety issue.
findings.rootCause: The loop couples attempt-all behavior to the separate rule that writes require every obligation to succeed.
findings.smallestPracticalCorrection: Attempt all pending obligations, retain sanitized per-command results/support references, then keep maintenance/read-only state and raise an aggregate error if any remain incomplete.
findings.broaderArchitecturalCorrection: None; do not quarantine obligations or re-enable writes automatically.
findings.regressionRisk: Medium: extra startup backup I/O and aggregate handling must not clear the fence early.
findings.verificationMethod: Multi-obligation first/middle/last and global-device failure tests; verify pending count, readiness, restart and write blocking until zero remain.
findings.uncertainty: If practical backup failures are always device-wide, the availability benefit is limited.
findings.falsePositiveNotes: The original permanent-blockage claim and P0 rating were not supported; fail-closed behavior is intentional and safe.
findings.releaseImpact: Optional recovery/diagnostic hardening after the current release.

findings.title: Pytest configuration still declares the removed backend runtime tree
findings.evidence: pytest adds backend to sys.path, no backend directory exists, and architecture explicitly says the obsolete backend runtime is absent. Actual package paths are bootstrapped by nicegui_app/__init__.py.
findings.impact: No current runtime outage; the config misstates topology and could silently make an accidental future backend directory importable only in tests.
findings.rootCause: Incomplete cleanup after migration to the NiceGUI-only architecture.
findings.smallestPracticalCorrection: Remove backend from the pytest pythonpath list.
findings.broaderArchitecturalCorrection: Add a repository-hygiene assertion that retired runtime roots stay absent and out of active import configuration.
findings.regressionRisk: Low; any hidden test dependency would correctly fail.
findings.verificationMethod: pytest collection/full suite, direct launcher smoke and repository documentation tests.
findings.uncertainty: None about the stale path; no broken current import was found.
findings.falsePositiveNotes: Classified P3 because the current suite and runtime pass.
findings.releaseImpact: Safe small cleanup; not a release blocker.
